neighbours.label: A word that introduces an inclusion or exception to a set just named ('including', 'except', 'excluding'), vs the same sentences listing the items directly
fire: The museum displays many artifacts, including tools, coins and pottery.
All the rooms were repainted (except the attic and the cellar).
The fee covers every service, excluding parking and meals.
The kit has everything you need, including a pump, gloves and a manual.
Every store in the chain will close early, except the one at the airport.
Several fruits are grown here, including figs, plums and apricots.
The offer applies to all items, excluding sale goods and gift cards.
The whole team attended (except the goalkeeper, who was injured).
quiet: The museum displays tools, coins and pottery from the region.
The attic and the cellar were left unpainted this year.
Parking and meals cost extra at the conference.
The kit has a pump, gloves and a short manual.
The store at the airport will stay open late tonight.
Figs, plums and apricots are grown in the valley.
Sale goods and gift cards can be returned within a week.
The goalkeeper missed the match because he was injured.

predictions: Introducers reach 0.3-0.8; direct lists stay under 0.1.
notes: Probe: 'including shelter' 0.81, '(except shopping' 0.74, 'outcompeting' 0.39, 'badly in' 0.23; direct list 0.04. Card peaks are mixed (Stub, Arabic له, his); this covers only the inclusion/exception part. 'excluding' untested.
